author: Anselmus Laudunensis et schola
issue: Corpus Corporum's TEI dropped the Hebrew type Migne sets inline before each Latin transliteration in the onomastic gloss on Lv 10:4. Recovered from the plate and re-inserted into both twins. See hebrew-recovery.md.

source.note: PL 113 leaf map f = (column + 1) / 2, calibrated against the printed corner numbers on every leaf read. Native page 1908x3118 (~300 ppi); that is the ceiling, anything larger is interpolation. A User-Agent header is required.

patches.note: Unpointed, as Migne sets it; MT has מִישָׁאֵל. Read at a 1900px native blow-up of the bottom of the left column. Migne's own transliteration Misael is the on-plate control. Pattern 13a clause 1: the loss left the sentence sound, so no [ed:] was fired when the gloss was translated.

Unpointed; MT has אֶלְצָפָן. Same read as the preceding entry. Migne's transliterations Elisaphan / Elzaphan are the on-plate control. The insertion point precedes a <pb n="0326A"/> falling inside the gloss; the Hebrew stands with Elisaphan in col 0325D, before the break.

notLacuna: No other Hebrew was dropped in this work. The only other non-Latin type is the Greek at 0339C and 0320A, both handled as TEI patches (diacritics and a rho misread as a mu), and the book-title line at the head of the work, recovered separately as <head type="book-title"> with ויקרא.
